request.description: Characterize bounded-effort reach, braking, settling, and complete-hold feasibility across the full official target geometry before choosing a learning intervention.
request.rationale: The scientific model establishes kinematic reach but leaves effective acceleration, braking margin, branch asymmetry, and hold stability unknown. A deterministic bounded joint-space PD probe over all official radii and angles, both feasible IK branches, and three damping schedules discriminates whether the first bottleneck is physical settling authority or policy learning and radial coverage.

request.current_goal_gap: No learned policy or candidate exists, and no evidence yet estimates episode success under the official distribution. The main gap is whether PPO can learn velocity-aware braking and stable 2-second holding across the omitted inner training radii, rather than whether the robot is kinematically or dynamically incapable of the task.
request.current_synthesis: Established model facts predict that bounded motor effort, residual velocity, and the 100-sample hold make stabilization consequential. M1 observed 60/60 grid targets with at least one feasible IK branch and 52/60 with both branches; a known-target joint-space controller completed 236/336 branch/gain trials (70.2%). The moderate soft and balanced schedules each completed 112/112 trials (100%) across all tested radii, both branches when feasible, and the full 100-step hold, with low median saturation (0% and 1.4%). The firm schedule completed only 12/112 (10.7%) and had 96.5% median saturation, showing that excessive command authority can destroy settling through saturation rather than reveal unreachable geometry. This supports physical feasibility with an appropriate braking regime and makes learning/coverage the leading bottleneck. Competing explanation: branch choice or configuration-dependent coupling could still cause failures for a learned policy despite the coarse PD grid; M1's matched open/folded results reduce but do not eliminate that possibility. Limits: M1 used known IK targets, 60 deterministic geometry points, and hand-selected PD gains; it is not evidence of learned-policy generalization or 98% official success.
request.decision_frontier: Can a learned policy acquire a stable velocity-aware reach-and-hold controller over the full official 6–20 cm radius distribution, or does PPO still fail specifically on inner-radius geometry, branch selection, or near-target braking? Discriminating evidence is a fresh 120000-step training run using full official radial coverage, followed by research evaluation with hold-specific episode evidence; success concentrated outside 14 cm would support the coverage explanation, while broad failures despite coverage would redirect toward policy representation, reward shaping, or control-method design.
request.human_goal_connection: The complete hold, not brief target entry, is the human objective. M1 directly tested the official 100-step hold outcome across the official radius and angular support, so it establishes whether the physical system has a credible route to the required behavior before spending training allocation.
